fields.mechanism: Clearance between the flat-faced follower and its guides induces impact forces and non-linear dynamic motion that amplify surface contact stress.
fields.intervention: Apply the paper's clearance-impact analysis to quantify and minimize the guide clearance on the fixed 16 mm follower studs, eliminating impact-induced peak loads while retaining the certified cam profile and 420 cycles per minute speed.
fields.expected_effect: Eliminating clearance-driven impacts reduces peak Hertzian contact stress below the fatigue threshold of the follower material, preventing surface spalling for longer than the required one-week maintenance interval and stopping food-contact metal contamination.
fields.falsification_test: Measure follower guide clearance before and after shimming; run the station at 420 cycles per minute for 9 weeks and inspect followers for spalls — if spalling persists at reduced clearance, the mechanism is falsified.
fields.mechanism_source_span: The system has clearances between the flat-faced follower and the guides and the effect of clearance is analyzed.

fields.mechanism: Clearance between the flat-faced follower and its guides introduces impact and friction that drive non-linear, chaotic motion, increasing dynamic contact stress on the follower face.
fields.intervention: Invert the active clearance-driven impact into a passive structural constraint by eliminating guide clearance; install zero-clearance preloaded split bushings on the fixed 16 mm studs to passively suppress follower tilt and lateral shift without altering the certified cam profile or operating speed.
fields.expected_effect: Suppressing clearance-induced non-linear impacts stabilizes the contact patch, eliminates localized Hertzian stress spikes, prevents surface fatigue spalling within the 6-9 week window, and stops metal debris contamination while satisfying the once-per-week maintenance limit.
fields.falsification_test: Mount an accelerometer on the follower stud and measure vibration spectra before and after installing zero-clearance bushings at 420 cycles per minute; if the largest Lyapunov exponent of the follower displacement does not decrease and spalling persists past 9 weeks, the intervention is falsified.

fields.mechanism: Clearance-induced non-linear impact dynamics between the flat-faced follower and its guides, analyzed via the largest Lyapunov exponent to characterize chaotic vibration that amplifies contact stress and drives surface fatigue spalling.
fields.intervention: Apply the paper's non-linear dynamic simulation framework to quantify the existing clearance between the 16 mm follower and its fixed stud guide, then install precision-matched guide bushings to eliminate the clearance driving the chaotic impact, while simultaneously applying a magneto-rheological fluid film at the cam-follower interface that uses an applied magnetic field to dynamically stiffen the lubricant viscosity in phase with the measured impact peaks, combining mechanical clearance elimination (tribology) with active magnetic damping (electromagnetism).
fields.expected_effect: Eliminating the guide clearance removes the chaotic impact excitation identified by the Lyapunov analysis, reducing peak Hertzian contact stress below the spalling fatigue limit, while the magneto-rheological film provides synchronized viscous damping of residual high-frequency vibrations, extending follower service life beyond the required weekly maintenance interval and preventing metal debris generation.
fields.falsification_test: Mount a high-resolution optical marker on the follower stem as described in the paper to measure y-direction displacement at 420 cycles per minute before and after intervention; if the largest Lyapunov exponent does not decrease to zero or negative values, or if surface spalling recurs within 9 weeks under continuous 20-hour daily operation, the mechanism is falsified.
